model_annotation: This bar chart, labeled Figure 10, illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating the standard deviation. The horizontal axis displays eight language family categories in the following order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, with the axis labeled "family." The vertical axis is labeled "effect" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. For each language family, a group of six bars is presented, corresponding to six model variants as indicated in the legend: mBERT-L₂ (dark blue), XLM-L₂ (dark green), mBERT-R₂ (medium red/pink), XLM-R₂ (medium green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink/salmon), and XLM-B₂ (light gray/beige). The IE-Baltic family shows some of the tallest bars, with several bars reaching approximately 20–25, while the Uralic family displays relatively short bars, mostly near or below 5. IE-Germanic bars range roughly from about 5 to 20, with notable variation across models. IE-Indic bars are generally moderate, clustering around 10–15. IE-Romance shows bars reaching approximately 15–22, with some of the taller values in the chart. IE-Slavic bars are moderate, roughly in the 10–20 range. IE-other shows moderate values around 10–15. Isolate bars are relatively moderate, around 10–18. Semitic bars range roughly from 5 to 15. Many of the bars display substantial error bars, indicating considerable standard deviation, particularly for IE-Baltic, IE-Romance, and Isolate families. The bars within each group are arranged side by side in the order matching the legend, and no specific sorting pattern (such as ascending or descending) is applied across the language families. No bars appear to be visually emphasized through bolding or outlining beyond the standard color coding.
